name: Lyman R. Sherman
role: One of the first presidents of the Seventy
dateNote: He became a president of the Seventy on 28 February 1835; section 108 dates from 26 December 1835.
importance: Section 108 answers his request to know his duty and says his sins are forgiven. It tells him to wait to be remembered with the first elders. He was called to the Twelve in January 1839 but died at Far West before he was told or ordained.
connections: He married Delcena Didamia Johnson in 1829. He served with the other presidents of the Seventy called in 1835.

sources.title: Lyman Royal Sherman, Joseph Smith Papers biography

reviewNote: JSP: born 22 May 1804, Monkton, Vermont; baptized Jan. 1832; Camp of Israel 1834; president of the First Quorum of the Seventy 28 Feb. 1835; Kirtland high council 1837; called to the Twelve 16 Jan. 1839; died c. 15 Feb. 1839, Far West. Section 108 calls him only “Lyman”, which also names Lyman Wight (124:22), so no linkNames.
